audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says four separate times that Maokai out-sustains Zac, but never says what actually drives Sap Magic.
audit.why: Sap Magic's cooldown is reduced "each time Maokai casts a spell OR IS STRUCK BY AN ENEMY'S SPELL". Zac's W is a flat 5-second AoE pulse and his whole pattern is spell spam - so Zac pouring abilities into Maokai is directly accelerating the heal he is trying to out-grind. This inverts the obvious plan. The answer is not to out-spam the sustain war, it is Grievous Wounds and short committed bursts, which is also why the full layer's "anti-heal stays core" line is right for a reason it never states.
audit.corrected: Added to spikes[0].text, mid and wants.you[2].
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json (P "Each time Maokai casts a spell or is struck by an enemy's spell, this cooldown is reduced")

audit.whatIsWrong: content spikes[0].text calls Sapling Toss his W ("his W (Sapling Toss) poke"), then in the same sentence correctly calls Twisted Advance his W. content early repeats it as "his saplings (W poke)".
audit.why: Sapling Toss is E. Twisted Advance is W. One sentence assigns the same slot to two different abilities, so the reader cannot tell which cooldown they are being told to track - and the two are nothing alike: E is an 1100-range zoning throw on 18s, W is a 525-range untargetable gap-close on 14s.
audit.corrected: Sapling Toss labelled E in spikes[0].text and early.
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json (E Sapling Toss range 1100 cd 18/17/16/15/14, W Twisted Advance range 525 cd 14/13/12/11/10)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing notes that Twisted Advance makes Maokai untargetable while it travels.
audit.why: He is untargetable for the duration of the dash, so Zac's Q is a single-target grab that simply cannot be used as the answer to his engage. The entry advises "Save E to dodge or punish his W root" without mentioning that the obvious Q counter is unavailable during the very window it would be wanted.
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json (W "becoming untargetable and dashing to the target")

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Maokai 5 stages and Zac none, in the matchup Zac wins hardest in this slice - 65.75%.
audit.why: Zero stages for the side winning by 15.75 points is the most extreme chart/data inversion here. The content layer even admits the tension in its own mid text ("your 65% win rate here reflects your edge in roaming"), so the entry knows the number and the chart still contradicts it. Maokai does own the early sustain war, so the fix is to end his run where anti-heal and Zac's scaling actually arrive.
audit.corrected: Maokai / Maokai / Maokai / Skill / Skill / Zac / Zac.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text and whys[4] say the two ultimates simply match, "so neither snowballs the other".
audit.why: Nature's Grasp is 130/110/90 against Let's Bounce! at 120/105/90. Zac's is ten seconds shorter at rank 1 and five at rank 2, level only at rank 3. Early, Zac gets his engage back first - which is exactly the window where the chart currently gives Maokai everything.
audit.corrected: Stated in whys[4], spikes[1].text and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] sits in the First item slot but reads "At 6 your R matches his engage".
audit.why: Stage mismatch - the first-item card talks about level 6, so the item spike is never explained anywhere in the chart.
audit.corrected: whys[5] now covers the first item, which in this matchup is the anti-heal timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention that Sapling Toss is stronger in brush.
audit.why: His E is explicitly "more effective in brush", and top lane is the brush-heaviest lane on the map. That changes which side of the wave is safe to stand on and makes the tri-brush a zone he owns for free, which is a wave-management fact the entry never gives.

Don't fight into that; farm at range, respect the root by holding E, and soak harass with your passive.
edits.after: Maokai wins the early sustain war — saplings (E, and stronger in brush) plus Sap Magic top him off faster than your blobs regen, and from 3 his W (Twisted Advance) roots you for a free trade. He is untargetable through that dash, so your Q grab cannot answer it. Farm at range and hold E.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 stay his — his root-into-poke pattern and constant sustain grind you down if you contest CS carelessly. But once both of you hit 6 the lane evens out: your R (Let's Bounce!) and his R (Nature's Grasp) are comparable engage tools, so neither can hard-snowball the 1v1, and your 65% win rate here reflects your edge in roaming and jungle setups rather than winning trades.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 stay his — the root-into-poke pattern and constant sustain grind you down if you contest CS carelessly, and pulsing W at him backfires: every spell that strikes Maokai shortens Sap Magic's cooldown again. From 6 it turns: your R (Let's Bounce!) answers his R (Nature's Grasp) and comes back 10s sooner at rank 1, and your 65% win rate reflects that edge plus roams.

edits.before: With items it's a pure tank mirror — two utility engage champs with no solo kill pressure, so the game is decided by who lands their team ult and roams better. Use your stronger E-flash engage and gank threat to make plays around the map; the lane itself is a farm-and-skill standoff you're happy to take even.
edits.after: With items you pull ahead rather than level out — anti-heal switches off the Sap Magic engine that carried his laning, and your W burns percent max health against a champion who stacks exactly that. Use your stronger E-flash engage and gank threat around the map; take the even standoff in lane and win everywhere else.
